key_insight: The paper unifies distributional shift in reinforcement learning by tracing it to causal origins within the agent–environment process, bridging ID/OOD generalization and non-stationarity under one taxonomy.
engineering_relevance: This gives RL engineers a structured way to diagnose where shift comes from, predict robustness failures, and choose adaptation strategies based on whether the source is agent-driven or environment-driven.
method: Reformulates dataset shift for RL using the interaction-generating process of a POMDP.
Decomposes shift into state distribution, observations, policy, reward, transition dynamics, and shifted-time boundary.
Classifies shifts as internal, external, explicit, implicit, or hybrid to unify ID/OOD and non-stationary cases.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an evaluation framework that measures shift impact and adaptation using performance degradation and recovery metrics.
watch_item: The taxonomy is conceptual and depends on correctly attributing causal sources of shift, which may be difficult in partially observed or real-world systems.
paper_title: A Unified Causal-Origin Taxonomy of Distributional Shifts in Reinforcement Learning
